newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian court recommends Clabecq takeover.
newsitem.headline: Belgian court recommends Clabecq takeover.

text.p: A Belgian court ruled on Wednesday that currently it was impossible to re-start bankrupt steel maker Forges de Clabecq after a group of creditor banks rejected an interim salvage plan, Belgian media said.

Various radio stations said the commercial court in Nivelles made the decision during a brief session on Wednesday and recommended court-appointed receivers now focus on a search for a takeover candidate rather than liquidate the firm outright.
Clabecq was declared bankrupt in January after the government of Belgium's French-speaking Walloon region, a key shareholder, pulled the plug on the loss-making company.
Receivers had been trying to patch together a deal to keep the firm going for five months to fulfil a backlog of orders and find a buyer for the company as a going concern.
Workers took legal action to force the Walloon government and the creditor banks to come up with a rescue package.

The Walloon government, under pressure from the court, had agreed to come up with 225 million francs ($6.6 million) but only on condition that the banks came up with the same amount. The banks refused.

Some 2,000 families in the towns of Tubize and Rebecq, in an area which already resembles a post-industrial era wasteland, depend on Clabecq for work and unionists have fanatically been defending the jobs, even resorting to physical violence in some instances.

Clabecq's death sentence was signed in December when the European Commission rejected a regional aid plan, brandishing it as inadmissible state aid for a firm without a future in an industry suffering from overcapacity.
The Commission has offered help to the area to convert the industrial jobs into more viable ones, but no extra cash.
Clabecq shares were delisted from the Brussels bourse after the company was declared bankrupt.
Saddled with high costs, poor margins and low-quality products, Clabecq had strugged to survive in a cyclical industry marked by overcapacity and cheap imports from eastern Europe.

Other Belgian steel firms have so far been cool on the idea of a cooperation or merger with Clabecq, either because they are not interested in its products -- mainly heavy plate -- or because they have already found another partner.
Unlisted Usines Gustave Boel is en route for a joint venture with Hoogovens of the Netherlands, which says, UGB complements its own business.
Belgium's largest steelmaker Cockerill Sambre has ruled out partnerships with UGB or Clabecq.
